frequency_context.assumption: Signals are approximated by a stationary Poisson arrival process solely to judge whether zero events in 320 minutes is surprising.
failure_modes: Shock arrivals are regime-clustered rather than stationary.
Development frequency can overstate prospective frequency because of selection bias.
The short observation window contains only one market condition and all rows are outside U.S. regular hours.

live_canary_context.interpretation: BRENTOIL execution feasibility and empirical friction are established; neither retired route nor the new oil-shock mechanism has established live edge.

development_context.interpretation: Development frequency is sufficient to justify continued prospective observation, but stress economics and path quality do not support live promotion.

diagnosis.reason: The observer has only 320 completed decision-minutes. Zero signals has an approximately 76%-77% diagnostic probability under development-rate constant-arrival assumptions, and the largest observed move reached only 42.37% of the frozen threshold.
falsifiers: A materially longer source-correct window produces substantially fewer onsets than the frozen development frequency predicts.
Eligible decisions are present but absent from the journal or are retroactively introduced.
The provider/profile/config identity or decision-source contract changes.
Resolved prospective lifecycles are persistently negative under live-tail friction.
